commands.description: Sign in once, in your own browser; the session is sealed into an encrypted bundle you hold.
Run a job as the carried identity. The fingerprint gate must accept before any state is released.
If challenged, hold the live session for a streamed human handoff instead of closing it.
Destroy a bundle (and, when named with --key-file, its key material); leaves an Ed25519-signed deletion receipt.
Verify a signed run receipt: PASS, or FAIL naming the field that changed.
Run the MCP server exposing the profile_run tool.

description: Nephew is the profile layer for the sandbox providers you already use. It carries one logged-in browser identity — cookies, session state, a coherent fingerprint, and a pinned egress IP — into Modal, Steel, Browser Use, and Browserbase. It is not another sandbox and does not replace them: jobs still run on the user's provider, under the user's account. There is no Nephew account to create, no Nephew cloud in the middle, and no Nephew server ever holds a profile.

handoff.deadline: Absolute, computed on a monotonic clock at start; late arrival, reloads, reconnects, and wall-clock changes cannot extend it.
handoff.eventRecord: Counts and identifiers only: frames relayed, inputs forwarded, outcome. No frames, no keystrokes, no page content, no token.
handoff.onResume: The live state is captured and sealed into the owner bundle.
handoff.surface: Loopback-only page (this machine only) streaming the live session from CDP screencast frames, with mouse and keyboard input forwarded back.
handoff.unavailableReason: Modal's browser runs inside the sandbox and exposes no host-side CDP session to lend; a Modal run that needs a login returns the plain LOGIN_REQUIRED pause.
handoff.who: The profile bundle's designated human only; every route requires a per-handoff token bound to that human.

howItWorks: Capture once: the session is sealed into an encrypted bundle the owner holds — profile state, fingerprint recipe, pinned proxy reference. Keys never leave the owner's machine.

Run anywhere: the sandbox browser is measured against the recipe; the fingerprint gate must accept before any state is released — on mismatch, the run refuses. The egress IP is measured and recorded on every run; on Modal the browser launches through the pinned proxy, on Steel, Browser Use and Browserbase the session leaves from the provider's own egress.

Challenged: the run pauses with LOGIN_REQUIRED and, on Steel, Browser Use, and Browserbase, can hand the live session to the designated human; resuming captures the fixed session back into the same bundle.
Capture back: when the job ends, the live session is sealed back into the same bundle. One identity, no forks.

install.checksum: Download verified against the published SHA256SUMS before install; a mismatch aborts.
requires: For capture: Linux x86_64 (fingerprint-chromium is installed for you), or your own fingerprint-chromium build via OWN_STACK_CHROME_PATH

limits: A site can still challenge a run. When it does, the run pauses with LOGIN_REQUIRED; the live handoff is the recovery on Steel, Browser Use, and Browserbase, and on Modal the recovery is still re-capture and retry.

Browserbase sessions: the 5-minute timeout in a project's settings is the default when no timeout is requested; Nephew requests an explicit 1-hour window — measured granted in full, including a probe at the 21,600-second API maximum.
One dedicated IP per identity, per-profile by design.
The egress pin is applied where Nephew launches the browser itself (Modal); on Steel, Browser Use and Browserbase the session leaves from the provider's egress, and every run record says which.
A handoff is one designated human, one controller, on a loopback page — and it ends at its deadline whether the login is fixed or not.
No 'works on every site' claims. Every run is measured the same way and writes its own metrics record.
measuredProof: Same profile, owner's machine vs a Modal sandbox: identical fingerprints — all 10 measured elements, canvas included — with the pinned font pack in both environments.

Pinned egress, measured live: a Modal run egressed from the profile's own dedicated IP, exactly as pinned in its recipe, and the session was restored. The address itself is carried in the run's own metrics record.
Baseline restores: ~6.4 s on Steel, ~7.8 s on Browser Use, ~5.7 s on Browserbase; full Modal runs 10–27 s in-session.
0 login prompts, 0 MFA prompts across the Steel, Browser Use, Modal, and Browserbase proof runs.

howToBuy.byo: Get BYO at https://nephew.ai/#pricing (Stripe Checkout), then nephew login <key>.

providers.note: The same bundle and the same fingerprint gate run on all four supported providers. Provider accounts and keys are the user's own; Nephew never stores them. On Browserbase the bundle is the only state a session sees — Nephew never uses Browserbase Contexts, and sessions are created with the API key alone (no project id).

receipts.deletionReceipt: nephew revoke leaves an Ed25519-signed deletion receipt, independently verifiable.

runReceipt.signedWith: The owner's Ed25519 receipt-signing key — the same key that signs the deletion receipt.
runReceipt.verify: nephew receipt verify <file> — checks the signature and, on the owner's machine, that the signer is the owner's own key; PASS, or FAIL naming the differing field.

mcp.handoffHandle: On Steel, Browser Use, and Browserbase, the LOGIN_REQUIRED pause result carries the live handoff handle.

tagline: Your logged-in identity, in any agent sandbox.
